scope: Riot's 18.3 patch notes (no dated update yet) against the published 18.2b snapshot. The MetaTFT lookup (generated 2026-09-11) and the 79 character bins are byte-identical to 18.2b's; CommunityDragon's export moved to the live 16.19 client. See 18.3-review.md.

mappings.reason: Essence per lost player combat, Coven's cash-out economy: trait-effects.json gives Coven no combat effect and the dashboard reports it unmodeled, so no fight reads this row. The lookup's row has no column-2 breakpoint ([[1, 18], [3, 32], [4, 60]]), so column 2 read 18 where Riot's old value and both CommunityDragon exports (16.18 and 16.19, {de46577b} 18/25/32/60) say 25; the mapping writes all four columns. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) coven: '22 Essence per loss', '28 per loss', '35 per loss', '60 per loss'.

DefenderDefenseGain is the armor and magic resist trait-effects.json gives a Defender at 2/4/6 Defenders (columns 1-3); it held exactly Riot's old 25/60/120. Column 4 (99) lies past the last breakpoint and is not in Riot's line. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) defender: 'Defender Defense Gain | 0 | 25 | 60 | 115 | 99'. The live 16.19 client export (CommunityDragon, game version 16.19.8207193) still carries the 18.2 value here, as it does for every 18.3 trait number but Invoker's; see 18.3-review.md.

TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) hunter: 'Hunter Attack Damage | 0% | 20% | 30% | 40% | 60%'. The live 16.19 client export (CommunityDragon, game version 16.19.8207193) still carries the 18.2 value here, as it does for every 18.3 trait number but Invoker's; see 18.3-review.md.

HPBurnPerSecond is the burn Inferno damage applies (trait-effects.json burnOnHit, which scales the row by 0.01, so the row keeps whole percents); it held exactly Riot's old 1/1/3.5/4.5, the values the 18.2 review mapped. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) inferno: 'Health Burn Per Second | 0 | 1 | 1 | 3 | 4'. The live 16.19 client export (CommunityDragon, game version 16.19.8207193) still carries the 18.2 value here, as it does for every 18.3 trait number but Invoker's; see 18.3-review.md.

InvokerManaBonus is the mana regeneration an Invoker gets on top of TeamManaRegen (trait-effects.json stats.manaRegen sums the two rows); it held exactly Riot's old 3/4/6/9. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) invoker: 'Invoker Mana Bonus | 0 | 3 | 4 | 6 | 8'. SOURCE CONFLICT, left open: the live 16.19 client files (CommunityDragon's en_us export and map22.bin, DA_18_Invoker variable {de27cb95}, which the trait tooltip prints as @InvokerManaBonus@ and which held 3/4/6/9 in the 16.18 export) now say 2/3/5/8, one less at every breakpoint, where Riot's note lowers only the last. The note is applied: it is Riot's primary statement for this patch, TFTraits agrees with it, and the same export demonstrably lags the server on this patch (Defender, Hunter, Inferno and Coven still show their 18.2 values there). If the client's 2/3/5/8 is what the server runs, an Invoker regenerates one mana a second less than modeled at 2-4 Invokers.

Quest economy, read by no fight. Riot's thousands separator keeps this mapping from becoming a reusable numeric encoding, so a later change to it needs its own review.

The AD form's stats block attack damage; it held Riot's old 45. The engine takes the AD form's base attack damage from its AutoAttackDamage row, mapped with it from this line. TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) gromp, Adaptor AD form stats: '50 Attack Damage'.

tft.kit_spec reads an AD form's base attack damage from its own AutoAttackDamage row at star 1 (then x1.5 a star), so this is the value the fights use. The row held 45/67.5/101.25/151.875, the base times 1, 1.5, 2.25 and 3.375; the new base scales the whole row by 50/45, the rule tft_update applies when a lookup's base attack damage moves (_DefinitionReview.curve, inherited_ad), and the 18.2 review's base-AD mappings (Warwick, Kha'Zix, Brambleback) wrote the same series. Star 4 is that derivation, stated by no source; nothing enumerates it. The unit-level AutoAttackDamage and stats (the AP form attacks with AutoAttackDamageAP, 30) are not in Riot's line.

note.text: Blackthorn Trait description displays incorrect stats at level 6 and does not say it sacrifices the unit. It does. But you get a lot of stats.

dispositions.reason: The trait's description text at 6 Blackthorn; Riot confirms the sacrifice happens and names no number. The sacrifice is unmodeled (trait-models: the sacrifice hex is left empty) and the description is presentation.

note.text: Finally found out the source of an issue where PvE units were entirely missing from a PvE round and fixed it. Thanks for the reports on this one, it was tricky to hunt down with how sporadic it was.

dispositions.reason: PvE rounds are not simulated; the fights use derived stat dummies, not monsters.

note.text: Fixed an issue where the minimize UI button can void selected Augment when clicked right after the Augment selection phase

dispositions.reason: Client interface during augment selection; no augment enters the model.

note.text: Fixed an issue where the Chat Box would collapse upon opening and clicking the scroll bar

dispositions.reason: Client interface.

note.text: MOBILE: Fixed an issue where the Main Menu music continued to play when signout out and going back to the title screen

dispositions.reason: Mobile client audio.

note.text: Fixed an issue where the Primal Urge mission provided inconsistent resulting towards progress

dispositions.reason: Mission (account progression) tracking; no fight, unit, item or trait is named.

note.text: MOBILE: Units on the bench can now be dragged as normal when the Augment Armory is open on certain devices that had issues before

dispositions.reason: Mobile client input.

note.text: Re-added a Ping Latency indicator to track data packet delivery times

dispositions.reason: Client network display.

note.text: Fixed an issue where certain Armories could overlap with the Shop after reconnecting back to a match

dispositions.reason: Client interface after reconnecting.

note.text: Fixed an issue where Units sold by dragging and dropping them above the XP/Reroll UI would sometimes fail to be sold.

dispositions.reason: Client input when selling.

note.text: Fixed an issue where the player would sometimes fail to return to their respective board after disconnecting and then reconnecting to a game

dispositions.reason: Client reconnection.

note.text: Fixed an issue with Champion Death animations ending abruplty after finishing a combat round

dispositions.reason: Animation playback after combat.

evidence: Riot 18.2, SEPTEMBER 14 update: 'Maokai Mana: 30/90 ⇒ 30/100'.
TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) maokai: '0/100Mana'.
CommunityDragon's export of the live 16.19 client (fetched with this candidate): 90 (16.18: 90).

sourceDisagreements.reason: Riot's September 14 update raised the bar to 100 and no later note moves it. The 16.19 client export still has 90, as it still has the 18.2 values of four trait rows 18.3 changes (see 18.3-review.md); the lookup, generated before that update, has 90 too.

evidence: Riot 18.2: 'Master Yi AD Form: Base AD: 65 ⇒ 60'; no 18.2 update or 18.3 line mentions it.
TFTraits (third-party, tftraits.com, page saved 2026-09-23) master-yi, AD form stats: '60Attack Damage'.
MetaTFT lookup (generated 2026-09-11, unchanged since 18.2b): 60.
CommunityDragon's export of the live 16.19 client (fetched with this candidate): 62; the 16.18 export had 65, the value before Riot's 18.2 change.
sourceDisagreements.reason: The client export moved from Riot's pre-18.2 65 to 62, a value no Riot note states. 60 is kept: Riot's own 18.2 statement, the lookup and TFTraits agree on it, and on this patch the same export disagrees with Riot's notes elsewhere (Invoker's mana, four trait rows still at 18.2 values). If 62 is live, AD Master Yi's attacks are about 3% stronger than modeled. Open.
